title: Juniper and the Protocol
premise: Edmund Nakamura, an insurance investigator who catalogues the colony of Meridian's impossible accidents, is the sole keeper of a beacon whose original commission records were erased. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream—a voice counting down beneath the ice—she traces it to the beacon and discovers it is a cryosleep triage protocol: only half of humanity's frozen sleepers can be revived before the reactor fails. The dream is the beacon's way of choosing, and the children's parents, including the colony council she answers to, want the choice made for them. Edmund must decide whether to obey her hidden directive to save the genetically privileged sleepers or follow the truth the children's shared dream reveals: that the beacon's designer encoded the choice in love, not lineage—and she must burn her own records, and her anonymity, to let everyone wake.
about_author: Coral Thackeray is a former marine salvage surveyor who spent six years cataloguing derelict stations before turning to fiction. She writes in the pre-dawn hours from a houseboat on the Salish Sea, where the fog does most of her world-building.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund files her 400th report on Meridian's statistically absurd accidents—falls, freezes, vanishings—all clustered near the beacon tower she alone maintains. Her supervisor, Councilor Voss, presses her to close the file and forget the tower. That night, her neighbor's daughter recites coordinates in her sleep: the beacon's own. Emotional beat: the unease of a woman who has built a life on not asking questions.

chapters.title: What the Children Count Down
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, with interludes from the dream itself. Dozens of children now share the dream—a voice beneath the ice counting from ten thousand. Edmund decrypts the beacon's erased commission record and finds the Protocol: the reactor will fail in ninety days, and the beacon must choose which half of the cryosleep vault wakes. The accidents were the beacon testing the colony, one impossible event at a time. Emotional beat: vertigo—her invisible duty is the colony's fate.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Mercy
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Voss discovers what Edmund knows and reveals the directive she was sworn to: save the genetically screened sleepers, the 'verified lineage.' The council moves to seize the beacon, and the children's dream begins counting faster. Edmund's ally, the archivist Ilsa Reyes, is arrested for helping her. At the climax, Edmund stands at the beacon console with the override key, both lists loaded, as Voss's security team breaches the tower. Emotional beat: love against duty, weaponized.

chapters.title: Wake Everyone or Wake No One
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, closing with the children's collective voice. Edmund refuses both lists and rewrites the Protocol using the beacon's own logic: the accidents were never tests of worthiness but lessons—each survivor of an impossible accident was proof that the colony could carry its frozen dead. She triggers a full revival at half-power, betting the children's shared dream is the beacon teaching the whole colony to hold the load. It works, barely. Voss is exposed by the records Edmund burns to save. Emotional beat: loyalty to truth over loyalty to orders; visibility as sacrifice.
